bpf_lsm.not_a_capability_gate: CAP_BPF, CAP_SYS_ADMIN, CAP_MAC_ADMIN, CAP_PERFMON all effective; only CAP_SYS_RESOURCE dropped; Seccomp=0
bpf_lsm.invariant_to: attach_btf_id in {0, bpf_lsm_file_open}; expected_attach_type in {0, BPF_LSM_MAC}
bpf_lsm.attribution: kernel lockdown reads `none [integrity] confidentiality`; integrity mode is the only active policy separating the two refused BTF-attached, kernel-memory-reading program types
bpf_lsm.residual_uncertainty: the probe did not toggle lockdown, so the specific kernel check was not isolated. selinuxfs is not mounted.
bpf_lsm.consequence_for_the_record: This changes the KIND of conclusion, not just its value. The addendum recorded CONFIG_BPF_LSM as NOT SET on 6.18.44-fc-v24, making the active-interception tier architecturally unavailable. Here the option is set, the bpf_lsm_* hooks are in BTF, bpf is in the active LSM list, and loading is refused by HOST POLICY. Correct status: DEPLOYMENT-GATED, not architecturally unavailable. External phrasing stays 'designed to support' until the probe is run on a lockdown-off host.
bpf_lsm.enforcement_stage_not_reached: Stage B would have denied a connect and required recovery after detach. It never ran because the load was refused first. It is retained and bounded three ways: one connect attempt, a link fd the kernel releases on close, and a forked child so even a crash releases it.
